transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… thanks for seeing me. I guess what brought me in is, at work I keep sort of… starting things and not fully finishing them. Like the sanitation steps, batch logs, end-of-line paperwork—I’ll do most of it, and then somehow the last parts get missed, even though I really do know they’re important and that my job depends on getting them right. It’s embarrassing, because I’m not trying to be careless. Does that make sense?
Have you had this same kind of trouble finishing tasks since childhood?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I did okay in school, so I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible student or anything. But my mom still has some of my elementary report cards, I think from around fourth grade, where the teachers wrote that I was bright but needed a lot of reminders to finish classwork and turn in homework.

I remember understanding what we were learning, but if the teacher wasn’t kind of right there or repeating things, I’d miss parts of the instructions and then not finish everything. Does that count as the same kind of thing?
Do these same kinds of problems with finishing things happen in your life outside of work too?

Um… outside of work, I guess it’s there too, but the work stuff is the clearest example. Like I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs and end-of-line paperwork, and I really do mean to finish them correctly, but somehow the last parts get left out. 

I know that’s still work, sorry—outside of work it feels similar, just maybe less obvious because there aren’t formal steps. But yes, it’s that same pattern of starting something and then not quite following through all the way. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you often get distracted easily when you’re trying to finish a task?

Yeah… I think I do. I try not to, and I’ll start a shift kind of telling myself, like, “Okay, stay focused, don’t mess this up.” But after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels kind of all blend together.

Sometimes I’ll notice I’m just staring at the same tray or the log sheet, and I haven’t actually taken in what I’m supposed to do next. It’s not like I’m trying to drift off… it just happens, I guess. Is that the kind of distraction you mean?
At home, do these attention problems make it hard for you to finish everyday tasks?

Yeah… I think it does, though honestly the thing that made me finally come in is more the work side of it. Like I’ll start the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and I know I have to finish every part correctly because my job depends on it.

But somehow I’ll get most of it done and then leave out the last parts. I don’t mean to be careless. It’s just like I start it, and then the follow-through at the end kind of falls apart. I’m sorry, I know you asked about home—at home it’s similar, but the work examples are the clearest for me.
Do you often feel nervous or unable to stop worrying?

Um… I don’t know that I’d say “often,” exactly. I mean, I get nervous about messing things up, especially when I know something matters, but I’m not sure if it’s the kind of worrying you mean.

I can worry, yeah, but I don’t think of myself as someone who’s just constantly unable to stop. Maybe I’m downplaying it a little—I’m not sure. What would count as too much worrying?
Have these attention problems caused serious difficulties in your home life too?

At home… I mean, it does make things harder, but I don’t want to exaggerate it. The serious problems are honestly more at work.

There it’s gotten bad enough that I’ve had formal retraining meetings, and sometimes coworkers have to cover parts of what I was supposed to do. That’s really embarrassing to say. I’m worried they’re going to move me off the line, or just fire me.

I feel like I’m starting to be seen as a safety concern instead of someone reliable, which is… kind of awful. So at home, yes, it affects me, but the part that feels serious is mostly work. Is that still okay to answer that way?
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I try to organize things, and sometimes I think I have a plan, but I don’t know if that counts as “trouble organizing” exactly.

Could you maybe say what you mean by organizing tasks? Like do you mean planning the steps, keeping track of what order to do things in, or actually finishing it that way?
When a task has several steps, do you often have trouble figuring out the order to do them in?

I’m not sure… I don’t always think of it as not knowing the order. Sometimes I can figure out what should come first if I stop and really think about it.

But if there are a lot of steps, I can get kind of unsure or second-guess myself, like, “Wait, was I supposed to do this before that?” I don’t know if that’s what you mean. It’s not like I can never do it, but it can get messy, I guess.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Um… I don’t think so? Not really depressed, I guess. I mean, I get stressed and embarrassed about things, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down in that way.

Unless you mean something broader by depressed? I just don’t want to answer it wrong.
When you’re trying to finish something, do little things around you easily pull your attention away?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but even when I start my shift really trying to stay focused, after a while the cutting, weighing, and checking labels kind of blur together.

Like, I’ll realize I’ve been staring at the same tray or the log sheet and I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next. I guess little things can pull me off, or sometimes it’s just… my attention slips. Does that answer what you mean?
When you’re doing something you find genuinely interesting, do you still have trouble staying focused all the way through?

I think… yes, sometimes. If it’s something I genuinely like, I can do better, but I wouldn’t say I’m always focused all the way through.

Like at work, even when I start a shift really trying to stay locked in and do everything right, after a while the cutting, weighing, and checking labels all kind of blur together. Then I’ll notice I’ve been looking at the same tray or the log sheet and not really taking in what I’m supposed to do next.

I don’t know if that counts as the same thing, since work isn’t always “interesting,” but it’s more like even when I’m trying hard, my focus doesn’t always hold.
Do you often forget everyday things, like errands, appointments, or where you put things?

Yeah… I mean, I try to be careful, but I do lose things a lot, especially at work.

It’s usually little stuff I need on the floor, like my cut glove or marker, my badge, safety glasses… and I’ll be like, “I literally just had that in my hand,” and then I’m walking back through everywhere I was for like ten minutes trying to find it.

I feel kind of stupid saying that, because everyone misplaces things, but it happens to me pretty constantly. Does that count as what you mean?
Did these problems with attention and follow-through start before you began this job?

Yeah… I think it did, at least looking back. I don’t want to blame everything on school or make it sound dramatic, but my mom still has some of my elementary report cards, like around fourth grade, and they say stuff like I was bright but needed a lot of reminders to finish classwork or turn in homework.

I remember understanding the lesson okay, but if the teacher wasn’t kind of nearby or checking in, I’d miss pieces of the instructions and then not finish the way I was supposed to. So… I guess it wasn’t only this job. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Outside of work, have these attention problems ever caused serious problems in your daily life?

I’m not totally sure what counts as “serious,” honestly. I don’t think I’ve had, like, some huge disaster outside of work because of it… at least not that I can think of right now.

It’s more that I notice it in little ways, but I kind of try to work around it or just tell myself I need to be more organized. I’m sorry, I don’t know if that’s a helpful answer. Are you asking about things like bills or school or relationships, or more like safety-type problems?
Have these attention problems ever caused you to miss paying bills on time?

I don’t think so… not that I can really point to. I mean, I try to pay things when I see them, and I haven’t noticed a pattern of missing bills because of attention.

Maybe I’d have to think about it more, but no, I don’t think that’s been a big issue for me. Is that okay to say if I’m not totally sure?
Outside of work, have these attention problems ever caused trouble in a relationship?

I don’t think so… not in a way I can clearly say was because of my attention. I mean, I’m sure people have gotten annoyed with me before if I forgot something small or seemed distracted, but I don’t think it’s caused, like, a major relationship problem.

Maybe I’m underthinking it, but I don’t really have a specific example. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Outside of work, have these attention problems ever caused you to make an unsafe mistake, like leaving the stove on or almost causing an accident?

No, I don’t think so. Like, I can’t remember leaving the stove on or almost causing an accident because I wasn’t paying attention.

I mean, I’m sure I’ve had normal little distracted moments, but nothing unsafe that stands out to me. If there’s a specific kind of situation you mean, I can try to think about it more.
Before this job, did these attention problems ever get you in serious trouble at school?

Serious trouble… not like suspensions or anything like that, no. But I guess there were signs pretty early.

My mom still has some of my elementary school report cards, like around fourth grade, where teachers wrote that I was bright but needed constant reminders to finish classwork and turn in homework. I remember understanding the lessons okay, but if the teacher gave instructions, I’d miss parts unless they were kind of right near me or checking in.

I don’t know if that counts as “serious trouble,” but it was definitely something teachers noticed.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Not really, no. I mean, I don’t think of myself as someone who can’t sit still.

Sometimes I shift around or feel a little antsy if something is boring, but I don’t think it’s, like, a big thing for me. Is that what you mean by restless?

Not really, no. I mean, I don’t think of myself as someone who can’t sit still.

Sometimes I shift around or feel a little antsy if something is boring, but I don’t think it’s, like, a big thing for me. Is that what you mean by restless?

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient’s main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern of inattentive symptoms beginning in childhood and persisting into adulthood across more than one setting, with clear occupational impairment. Confirmed features include difficulty sustaining attention, incomplete follow-through, distractibility, forgetfulness/misplacing items, and some difficulty managing multistep tasks. Childhood onset is supported by elementary report cards noting repeated reminders to finish work and turn in homework. Anxiety appears secondary to work difficulties and does not meet clearer threshold from the interview for a primary anxiety disorder.
